properties.decision:
`gap_id` keys a gap on its RULE alone when the gap is an AGGREGATE — one per project, whose `affected_ids` are the whole population the rule ranges over rather than the nodes the finding is about. Every other gap keeps hashing its affected set. Today exactly one source qualifies: `unvalidated_capability`.

The discriminator is an explicit `GapSource::is_aggregate()` written as an exhaustive match, not a wildcard, so a future aggregate detector has to come to this function and decide rather than silently inheriting per-node keying.

NOT KEYED ON `GapScope::Project`, which is the obvious-looking answer and is wrong. `unsatisfied_requirement` and `status_contradiction` are project-SCOPED but carry a single requirement each, and `kpp_breached` is per-KPP. Keying on scope would collapse every unsatisfied requirement in the design into one gap sharing one judgement — accept one and the rest go silent. A test pins this specific trap (`a_project_scoped_but_per_node_gap_still_keys_on_its_subject`) and a mutation confirms it fails when the trap is taken.

Also NOT chosen: (b) expiring only when a member is removed, which keeps the id unstable and merely narrows when it moves; (c) letting each acknowledgement declare its own expiry condition, which is more machinery than the problem needs and puts the judgement about mechanism into every reason string; (d) modelling rollups as a different KIND of gap, which is a schema change for something the id function can express.
properties.name: An aggregate gap is keyed on its rule; every other gap still keys on its subject
properties.rationale:
Anthony's word, 2026-07-30: he was told the finding had a close sibling in the defect-side mechanism and said that was a good approach.

WORTH RECORDING PRECISELY, because the reading that prompted this was half wrong. The sibling was described as "defect acknowledgements expire by shape, and this is the gap side catching up". Reading the code showed `heal.rs`'s `issue_id(category, affected)` hashes its affected set exactly as `gap_id` does — the defect side has no cleverer keying. What it actually has is the `retired` REPORTING that `reviewed_gaps` already implements too. So mirroring the sibling alone would not have fixed anything: the churn comes from the id derivation, and the fix had to be there. The sibling still earns its place, because `retired` reporting is what makes a stable id safe — when the rule stops firing the standing review is shown as retired rather than silently kept.

THE TRADE-OFF IS REAL AND ACCEPTED. A stable id means a capability added later is covered by the earlier judgement without a fresh look. That is what a STANDING disposition means — "validation is tracked in the trials programme" is a claim about the practice, not about any one capability — and it is what the twenty re-acknowledgements were each re-asserting unchanged. The growth stays visible without the churn: a review records the count it was made at in its own reason, and the live gap's title carries the count now, so a reader comparing them sees the set grew.

THE MIGRATION IS DELIBERATE AND VISIBLE. The rollup's id moves once, from the member-hashed `gap:80f8bc457bfe9e16` to the stable `gap:0a77650b58242054`, so the twenty historical acknowledgements no longer match it and one fresh acknowledgement is needed — the last one this gap should ever need. Those twenty are left exactly as they are rather than withdrawn: withdrawal marks a Decision `superseded`, which would claim the judgement was revoked, and it was not. `reviewed_gaps` reports them as `retired` instead, which is the honest description — the judgement was real and the situation it named has moved on.
